title.en: Objectives of business and business risk

hook.en: A business that makes no profit cannot survive. But a business that cares only about profit soon loses its customers, its workers and its good name.

objectives.en: Explain the role of profit and the multiple objectives of business
Define business risk and state its nature
Classify the causes of business risk

narration.en: A business that makes no profit cannot survive. But a business that cares only about profit soon loses its customers, its workers and its good name.

body.en: Profit is essential: it is the reward for risk, a source of funds for growth, and a measure of efficiency. But a business pursues several objectives together: market standing (a strong position among competitors), innovation (new products and methods), productivity (more output for the same input), physical and financial resources (acquiring and using them well), earning profits, manager performance and development, worker performance and attitude, and social responsibility (to customers, workers, the community and the environment).

points.en: Profit: reward, growth fund, efficiency test

title.en: On the board: causes of business risk

say.en: Business risk is the possibility of inadequate profits or even losses due to uncertainties.

text.en: causes of business risk
Natural causes: floods, earthquakes, drought, fire
Human causes: dishonest employees, strikes, bad debts
Economic causes: changes in demand, prices, competition,
interest rates, technology
Other causes: political change, accidents, machine failure
It arises from uncertainty; it cannot be removed entirely
The degree of risk depends on the nature and size of
business

body.en: Business risks arise because the future is uncertain. They are an essential part of every business and cannot be eliminated, only reduced (by careful planning, research, diversification, insurance of insurable risks). The degree of risk depends mainly on the nature (fashion goods are riskier than groceries) and the size of the business (bigger operations, bigger risk). Profit is the reward for risk-taking: the greater the risk, the greater the possible profit. Some risks, like fire, are insurable; others, like a change in fashion, are not.

problem.en: Why should a business not aim at profit alone? Give four reasons.

steps.en: Customers will leave if quality and fair prices are ignored.
Workers who are exploited become less productive and may strike.
Neglect of innovation makes the firm fall behind competitors.
Ignoring society and the environment damages reputation and invites regulation.

answer.en: Long-run profit depends on balancing several objectives, not on profit alone.
